items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: Howard Johnson calls me up and he says, “Mingus is putting a band together, he wants to use tuba and baritone man, come on down to such and so and so.” I said, “Yeah, cool.” And so they put the big band together and we did two albums.

ctx.x: That time passed, I forgot how to do it wrong, and so when I picked it up I was doing it right, it worked. And Howard was doubling on flugelhorn and baritone saxophone and Joe Daly was tuba and valve trombone and Earl McIntyre was tuba and bass trombone. So we did that for the first four months of 1971, it was ’71. And then when that finished in April I was kind of like depressed because I mean it’s hard coming off one of those gigs where you’re playing for 5,000 people and 10,000 people, screaming and hollering,…
hire the band for that Avery Fisher Hall concert. And he was great to me, he was just as nice as he could be.
